rules.title: Santa Monica Rent Control Charter Amendment: maximum allowable rents and annual general adjustment
rules.requirement: Rents on controlled units cannot exceed the Rent Control Board's maximum allowable rent (MAR). Each year the MAR rises by 75% of the regional CPI change, but never less than 0% or more than 3%. Landlords may not raise rent if they are unregistered or have uncorrected housing-code violations.
rules.citation: Santa Monica City Charter art. XVIII, §§ 1804-1805
citation_aliases: Santa Monica Rent Control Charter Amendment
rules.quoted_span:
in no event shall the general
adjustment be less than zero percent or greater than three (3) percent
rules.effective_date_note: Rent control originally enacted 1979; the 0%-3% general adjustment limit (§1805(a)(3)) was amended 11/8/22, effective 12/6/22. That date is used.
rules.key_value: 75% of CPI, min 0%, max 3% annual general adjustment
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential rental units in Santa Monica except exempt units (hotels, institutions, owner-occupied up to 3 units, new construction after adoption of the Article, single family homes per §1815, etc.).
rules.exemptions: Transient hotel/motel units; hospitals, convents, dormitories; certain government-owned units; owner-occupied dwellings of 3 or fewer units; units constructed after adoption of the Article (not conversions); non-profit child care/social service units; single family homes to the extent in §1815 (not in this part). Exemptions are granted by the Board on owner application.
rules.penalty: Landlord who fails to register or comply may not increase rent; tenant may refuse to pay an improperly noticed increase.
rules.conflict_note: Adoption date of the Article is not stated in this document; the April 10, 1979 cutoff is inferred from the 1979 enactment and the April 10, 1979 reference in §1801(n). Single-family exemption (§1815) is outside this part.

unverifiable_exemptions: owner-occupied dwellings with 3 or fewer units
single family homes and condominiums (§1815)
government-owned or subsidized units
hotels, institutions, dormitories
non-profit child care/social service use

rules.title: Santa Monica Rent Control Charter Amendment: eviction only for just cause
rules.requirement: A landlord may not demand possession, threaten termination, serve a notice to quit, or sue to recover a controlled unit unless a listed ground applies, such as the tenant's failure to pay the rent lawfully due.
rules.citation: Santa Monica City Charter art. XVIII, § 1806
rules.quoted_span:
No landlord shall take action to terminate any tenancy including but not limited, to making a demand
for possession of a rental unit, threatening to terminate a tenancy, serving any notice to quit or
other eviction notice
rules.effective_date_note: Original 1979 enactment; this part shows only the start of §1806 (grounds after (a)(1) are cut off).
rules.key_value: Eviction of controlled units only on enumerated just-cause grounds
rules.coverage_conditions: Controlled rental units as defined in §1801(c).
rules.exemptions: Same exemptions as controlled rental units under §1801(c).
rules.conflict_note: Text truncated at §1806(a)(2); remaining grounds not in this part.

unverifiable_exemptions: owner-occupied dwellings with 3 or fewer units
single family homes (§1815)
government-owned or subsidized units

rules.title: Santa Monica Rent Control Charter Amendment: security deposits in interest-bearing accounts
rules.requirement: Security deposits and advance rent on controlled units must be held in an interest-bearing account at a federally insured institution until returned to the tenant or properly used. The landlord may pay the interest to the tenant or use it to offset operating expenses unless the Board orders it paid to tenants.
rules.citation: Santa Monica City Charter art. XVIII, § 1803(s)
rules.quoted_span:
shall be placed in an interest bearing account at a federally insured financial
institution until such time as it is returned to the tenant or entitled to be used by the landlord
rules.effective_date_note: Effective date of this subsection not stated in this part.
rules.exemptions: Same as controlled rental unit exemptions.
rules.interaction: Board may regulate amount and use of deposits consistent with state law.

unverifiable_exemptions: owner-occupied dwellings with 3 or fewer units
single family homes (§1815)
government-owned or subsidized units

rules.title: Santa Monica Rent Control Charter Amendment, Art. XVIII §1806 (Eviction for cause only)
rules.requirement: Landlords of controlled units may not demand possession, serve a notice to quit, or sue to evict unless one of the listed just causes applies (e.g., nonpayment, material breach after written notice to cease, nuisance, owner/relative move-in, demolition, Ellis withdrawal). The notice must state the cause and be filed with the Rent Control Board within 3 days (except 3-day pay-or-quit notices). Retaliatory evictions are barred. Owner move-in requires good-faith occupancy within 60 days for at least two years, with protections for tenants 62+ or disabled with 5+ years or terminally ill.
rules.citation: Santa Monica City Charter art. XVIII, § 1806
citation_aliases: Santa Monica Rent Control Charter Amendment
rules.quoted_span:
No landlord shall take action to terminate any tenancy including but not limited, to making a demand
for possession of a rental unit, threatening to terminate a tenancy, serving any notice to quit or
other eviction notice
rules.effective_date_note: Article XVIII adopted 4/10/79; §1806 last amended with effect 12/6/22 (used original adoption date for the core rule). Exact effective date of 1979 adoption not stated beyond adoption date.
rules.key_value: Eviction only for enumerated just causes; cause stated in notice; copy filed with Rent Control Board within 3 days
rules.exemptions: Applies to controlled rental units; single family homes not rented July 1, 1984 are exempt (§1815); State Park/tidelands property exempt (§1820).
rules.penalty: Wrongful eviction: actual and punitive damages, injunctive relief, attorney fees; misdemeanor (fine up to $500 and/or up to 6 months jail) under §1810.

unverifiable_exemptions: single-family homes not rented on July 1, 1984
State Park System / sovereign tidelands property
owner-occupied or other exemptions defined elsewhere in the Charter

rules.conflict_note: Applies to 'controlled rental units' as defined in other parts of the Charter (not in this part of the document); coverage may be uncertain.

rules.title: Santa Monica Rent Control Charter Amendment, Art. XVIII §1815 and §1820 (coverage exemptions)
rules.requirement: Single family homes not rented on July 1, 1984 are exempt from Santa Monica rent control; other single family homes are covered but can be permanently exempted after two years of continuous owner occupancy following a voluntary vacancy or lawful eviction. State Park and sovereign tidelands property is not covered.
rules.citation: Santa Monica City Charter art. XVIII, §§ 1815, 1820
citation_aliases: Santa Monica Rent Control Charter Amendment
rules.quoted_span:
Single Family homes that were not used for residential rental purposes on July 1, 1984 are automatically
exempt from the provisions of this Article
rules.effective_date_note: §1820 effective 12/10/90; §1815 adoption date not stated in this part.
rules.exemptions: Single family homes not rented July 1, 1984; owner-occupied single-family homes after 2 years; State Park/tidelands property.

unverifiable_exemptions: single-family homes not rented on July 1, 1984
owner-occupied single-family homes exempted by Board
State Park System / sovereign tidelands property

rules.conflict_note: Rent cap formulas are in the earlier part of the Charter; this part provides only coverage exemptions.

rules.title: Santa Monica Rent Control Regulation 14002: Ceiling on Security Deposit
rules.requirement: For controlled rental units, the security deposit generally cannot exceed the maximum allowable rent or base rent after vacancy on the initial rental date. Small landlords (natural person or all-natural-person LLC, owning no more than two properties with four or fewer units total) may demand two months' rent from non-service-member tenants. Once set, the deposit cannot be raised during the tenancy.
citation_aliases: Santa Monica Rent Control Regulations ch. 14
rules.quoted_span:
The landlord may
demand a security deposit in an amount equal to two months’ rent if the prospective tenant is not a
service member and both the following are true:
rules.key_value: 1 month's max allowable rent; 2 months for qualifying small landlords
rules.effective_date_note: Two-month small-landlord provision amended 8/8/24, effective 8/17/24; the original ceiling dates from 1983 (effective 12/7/83).
rules.exemptions: Applies to controlled rental units only.
rules.coverage_conditions: Controlled rental units under Santa Monica rent control.

unverifiable_exemptions: units not under Santa Monica rent control
coverage.landlord_size_condition: Two-month deposit only for a natural person or all-natural-person LLC owning no more than two residential rental properties with no more than four dwelling units total

rules.interaction: Total deposit cannot exceed the state maximum (see § 14003(c)).

rules.title: Santa Monica Rent Control Regulation 14001: Interest-Bearing Account
rules.requirement: Landlords must hold all security deposits in an interest-bearing account at an FDIC- or FSLIC-insured institution until the deposit is returned to the tenant or the landlord is entitled to use it.
rules.quoted_span:
All security deposits shall be placed in an interest-bearing account at an institution whose accounts are
insured by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation or the Federal Savings and Loan Insurance
Corporation
rules.key_value: Deposits must be held in an insured interest-bearing account
rules.conflict_note: Subsections (b)-(f) of 14001 were suspended 6/13/02; only subsection (a) is reproduced here.

rules.title: Santa Monica Rent Control: Maximum Allowable Rent, annual General Adjustment, registration-fee pass-through and property-tax surcharges
rules.requirement: Rent in controlled units is limited to the Maximum Allowable Rent (MAR), which rises by an annual General Adjustment (3.0% effective September 1, 2024). Owners who pay the registration fee on time may pass half through as a monthly surcharge ($9.50 for 2024/25). For tenancies that started before March 1, 2018, owners may pass through limited property-tax items, capped at $35 or 4% of the MAR, whichever is less.
rules.citation: Santa Monica Rent Control Law (Maximum Allowable Rent, registration fee and surcharge pass-throughs)
citation_aliases: Santa Monica Rent Control Board General Adjustment History & Surcharges
rules.quoted_span:
The total monthly pass-through of the five line items from the owner’s property tax bill may not
exceed $35 or 4% of the 2024/2025 MAR, whichever is less
rules.effective_date_note: The document gives no effective date for the underlying law. The 2024 General Adjustment took effect September 1, 2024.
rules.key_value: General Adjustment 3.0% (2024); surcharge cap $35 or 4% of MAR, whichever is less
rules.exemptions: The document does not list exemptions. The General Adjustment does not apply to units whose tenancy started on or after September 1 of the prior year. Property-tax surcharges apply only to tenancies that started before March 1, 2018. They end if the property is reassessed on or after March 1, 2018 because of a sale or voluntary improvements. Low-income tenants may have the tax surcharge waived.

unverifiable_exemptions: tenancy start date
low-income tenant waiver
owner age 65+ exemption from school parcel tax

rules.title: Measure RR – Charter amendment limiting nonpayment evictions (Rent Control Law Art. XVIII §1806(a)(1))
rules.requirement: If voters approve Measure RR, a landlord of a rent-controlled unit could not evict for nonpayment unless the amount owed exceeds the average HUD Small Area Fair Market Rent for an equivalent-size unit in Santa Monica ZIP codes, and the notice must state the bedroom count and that rent amount.
rules.citation: Santa Monica City Charter art. XVIII, § 1806(a)(1)
rules.quoted_span: provided that the amount due exceeds the average of the Small Area Fair Market Rents set annually by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development for equivalent sized rental units
rules.effective_date_note: On the Nov 3, 2026 ballot; not yet decided as of the document date.
rules.key_value: Nonpayment eviction only if rent owed exceeds average HUD Small Area FMR (about one month)
rules.coverage_conditions: Rent-controlled rental units under the Santa Monica Rent Control Law.
rules.interaction: Governs instead of Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2 for units under the Rent Control Law.

rules.title: Measure RR – Charter amendment limiting nonpayment evictions (Housing Policies Art. XXIII §2304(a)(1))
rules.requirement: If voters approve Measure RR, a landlord of a non-rent-controlled unit covered by the Housing Policies article could not evict for nonpayment unless the amount owed exceeds the average HUD Small Area Fair Market Rent for an equivalent-size unit, and the notice must state the bedroom count and that rent amount.
rules.citation: Santa Monica City Charter art. XXIII, § 2304(a)(1)
rules.quoted_span: provided that the amount due exceeds the average of the Small Area Fair Market Rents set annually by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development for equivalent sized rental units
rules.effective_date_note: On the Nov 3, 2026 ballot; not yet decided as of the document date.
rules.key_value: Nonpayment eviction only if rent owed exceeds average HUD Small Area FMR (about one month)

unverifiable_exemptions: single-unit dwellings and condominiums are excluded from the Housing Policies article

rules.coverage_conditions: Non-rent-controlled rental units, excluding single-unit dwellings and condominiums.

rules.title: Santa Monica algorithmic rental pricing software ban
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use, and vendors may not sell, algorithmic software that uses competitor data to advise on rent prices or whether to leave units vacant. Tenants can raise violations as an affirmative defense in eviction cases, and tenants or the city can sue; penalties are $1,000 per offense or actual damages, whichever is greater, plus attorney fees.
rules.citation: Santa Monica algorithmic rental pricing ordinance
rules.quoted_span: The Santa Monica ordinance defines prohibited "algorithmic devices" as software that uses competitor data to advise landlords on rent pricing or whether to leave units vacant
rules.key_value: ban on sale and use of algorithmic devices using competitor data
rules.penalty: $1,000 per offense or actual damages, whichever is greater, plus attorney fees
rules.effective_date_note: Article (published 2025-07-02) says the council adopted the ordinance 'last week'; no effective date stated.
rules.conflict_note: Ordinance number and section not given in the source; adoption date inferred from the article's 'last week' wording.
